data.title: Enerev5 Metals Inc. Adopts Semi-Annual Financial Reporting
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Toronto, Ontario – October 30, 2026 – TheNewswire - Enerev5 Metals Inc. (TSX-V: ENEV) (“Enerev5” or the “Company”) has adopted semi-annual financial reporting (“SAR”) pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 — Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers.

The blanket order allows eligible venture issuers listed on the TSX Venture Exchange to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework. By adopting SAR, the company aims to reduce the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting.

The Company's fiscal year ends on May 31. Under the SAR pilot program, the Company will no longer file interim financial reports and related management's discussion and analysis (MD&A) for its three-month and nine-month interim periods. The initial interim period for which the Company will not file is the three-month period ended August 31, 2026.

The Company will continue to file audited annual financial statements and MD&A (due 120 days after May 31) and unaudited six-month financial statements and MD&A (due 60 days after November 30).

The Company remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102 --Continuous Disclosure Obligations and the policies of the TSX-V.

This news release is being issued and filed pursuant to the blanket order.

About Enerev5 Metals Inc.

Enerev5 Metals Inc. (TSX-V: ENEV) is a Canadian exploration company focused on the identification and development of critical battery metals projects in stable, mining-friendly jurisdictions. The Company’s strategy is to build a portfolio of early-stage assets that have the potential to supply ethically-sourced metals essential to the global transition to clean energy. Enerev5 is currently advancing lithium exploration in northeastern Nevada and continues to evaluate additional opportunities in high-potential jurisdictions to support its long-term growth objectives.

data.title: Inside the largest crypto hack on record: How attackers breached Binance for $6.3 billion
data.description:
Binance was hit Thursday by the largest crypto hack to date, with blockchain investigators estimating that more than $6 billion in assets were stolen. Beyond the financial toll, the breach has raised questions about the security of centralized exchange infrastructure, particularly the hot wallets used to custody billions of dollars in customer assets.

Binance said its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop and unauthorized access to a service container. The exchange has not identified a private-key leak, while co-CEO Richard Teng has described the attack as more complex than a compromise of a single employee's permissions.

Blockchain investigators have attributed the attack to North Korean hackers. Their analysis suggests the attackers exploited Binance's internal systems and wallet-signing mechanisms to move funds across multiple blockchains.

How Binance was attacked

The attacker began staging at least 36 hours before the theft, funding an operational wallet with small Tornado Cash withdrawals, according to TRM Labs. It deployed and tested malicious code on three wallets before executing the attack.

On Ethereum, the attacker used EIP-7702 to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper controlled by the attacker. It prepared 50 pre-signed authorizations to ensure one would remain valid when executed. TRM said coordinated transfers across nine other blockchains suggest a compromise of Binance's broader hot-wallet signing infrastructure.

Elliptic's analysis suggests the attacker retained access beyond the initial exploit, using one compromised wallet's owner rights to withdraw funds from another Binance wallet and repeatedly sweep new deposits. A second Ethereum hot wallet also sent $174 million in assets directly to the attacker, further pointing to access to Binance's broader transaction-signing infrastructure.

Simone Imbrescia, vice president of Immunefi, said the exploit highlights how an attack's sophistication does not necessarily lie in its onchain code, but in gaining access to the infrastructure capable of authorizing transactions.

"One of the striking things about this breach is how little code was actually needed on-chain. The sweeper contract was only around 130 lines," Imbrescia said. "The hard part sometimes is getting access to a system powerful enough to make very simple code devastating."

Chainalysis, Elliptic, and TRM attributed the attack to North Korean hacking groups, with TRM explicitly linking it to the same group connected to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.

Chainalysis identified onchain links between funds stolen from Binance and proceeds from last month's Bitget exploit, which was also attributed to North Korean hackers. TRM cited similarities to previous North Korean operations, including Tornado Cash funding, advance staging and pre-signed authorizations. Elliptic also cautioned that the onchain overlap with the Bitget incident involved only a small portion of the Binance funds and did not conclusively establish that the same attackers were responsible.

Chainalysis identified thousands of transactions in a short period, with stolen funds repeatedly circulating between addresses. The attacker also attempted to avoid stablecoin freezes by converting $325 million in stablecoins into $285 million in ETH over nearly 20 minutes.

Elliptic said the attacker deposited $59.9 million in stolen USDT into Aave as collateral and borrowed 19,762 ETH. The loan remained open and was close to liquidation as of the firm's latest update. The attacker also swapped hundreds of millions of dollars in USDT for ETH through decentralized exchanges and market makers, accepting losses of as much as 26% against market prices to move funds into assets that issuers cannot freeze.

Aave said Friday that it had unfrozen all markets across its V3 and V4 protocols, adding that its smart contracts were unaffected and user positions remained fully collateralized.

Binance's financial position

Binance has approximately $5 billion in affected assets, with another $1.3 billion being acquired through market and OTC channels as part of its commitment to cover the losses.

Teng said the exchange was targeting Monday to publish its initial proof-of-reserves report and was working to restore withdrawals.

"We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to our Sunday deadline, which is on track to be within 40 hours," Teng said in an X video on Friday.

TD Cowen analysts said the breach highlights the custody and cybersecurity risks associated with centralized exchanges but does not necessarily undermine the broader digital asset industry.

"The evidence available so far points to a compromise of infrastructure at a centralized intermediary, rather than a failure of Bitcoin or its underlying network," the analysts wrote. "Put differently, we do not stop using dollars when a bank is robbed, just as car theft does not invalidate the automobile."

The incident also highlights the need to secure the systems and processes that control access to private keys, Imbrescia said. Crypto security efforts often focus on protecting keys and auditing smart contracts, but the people, infrastructure and workflows capable of instructing those keys are part of the security perimeter, she added.

"If an attacker compromises that operational layer, they may not need to steal a key or discover an exotic smart-contract vulnerability at all," she said. "The broader lesson is that access controls, internal infrastructure and transaction-authorisation processes need to be secured with the same intensity as the keys themselves."

data.title: VantageScore President, CEO Silvio Tavares Resigns
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

VantageScore President and Chief Executive Silvio Tavares is stepping down from his roles after leading the company for five years, the credit-scoring company said.

Anthony Hutchinson, who led the company's public affairs and government relations efforts, was named as interim president and CEO. VantageScore's board is conducting a formal leadership search, the company added.

Hutchinson joined VantageScore four years ago. Before that, he held senior positions at Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae and the National Association of Realtors, the company said.

VantageScore is an independent joint-venture company owned by Equifax, Experian and TransUnion.

Write to Stephen Nakrosis at stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com

data.title: Weil would join crowded field of defunct law firms
data.description:
By David Thomas

The fast-moving melt-down of Wall Street powerhouse Weil, Gotshal & Manges stunned even legal insiders who were tracking its fortunes closely. But it's just the latest in a string of notable law firms to fall apart in recent decades, as a mix of partner defections, debt or other factors have brought down once-stable firms.

Weil said this week it plans to wind down operations following a series of key partner departures that it could not stem, spelling the end of a 1,200 lawyer firm that generated more than $2 billion in revenue last year.

It would join at least seven other US law firms with at least 100 lawyers that have dissolved over the past 15 years, including the 2012 implosion of Dewey & LeBoeuf. With profits per equity partner of nearly $5.6 million last year, Weil was by all accounts financially healthy, and it would be the first top 25 firm by revenue since Dewey to collapse without securing a merger.

Some of the firms that dissolved in recent years have managed, as Weil intends, to wind-down their affairs outside of bankruptcy, while others ended up in court.

Either way, the process can go on for years. Howrey's bankruptcy case is still open after 15 years. Duane Morris' Leslie Corwin, who co-wrote a treatise on law firm partnerships, noted that he is still working on dissolving Philadelphia-based law firm Schnader Harrison Segal & Lewis, which closed its doors in 2023.

The dismantling of a law firm can be a wrenching process for the lawyers who worked there, as details such as partners' financial obligations and entitlements are hammered out, experts on the process said.

"It’s the equivalent of managing hundreds of divorces because people get really emotional," said Al Togut, who was lead counsel to Dewey when it filed for bankruptcy. "A lot of these folks could never imagine what’s happening now."

Weil in a statement said its management committee recommended an "orderly wind-down" to unfold in the coming months. During that time, "the firm will continue serving clients with the dedication and excellence that have defined it since its founding and will remain committed to supporting its ​colleagues," Weil said.

Here's a look at how some other recent law firm disintegrations played out.

STROOCK & STROOCK & LAVAN

New York-based Stroock voted to dissolve in October 2023 after a series of lawyer exits gutted its partnership and it failed to secure a merger with a larger firm. The firm began experiencing troubles in 2022 after nearly its entire restructuring group, which had generated 29% of the firm's revenue in 2021, decamped for Paul Hastings, a rival firm.

Stroock, which was founded in 1876, had merger discussions with other law firms such as Nixon Peabody and Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman prior to its dissolution.

Stroock had 222 lawyers and revenue of $250 million in 2022, according to The American Lawyer. The firm two years later announced a settlement with its major creditors, resolving its wind-down and asset distribution.

LECLAIRRYAN

Richmond, Virginia-based LeClairRyan voted to dissolve in August 2019 after a spate of partner exits and filed for bankruptcy a month later. The firm revealed in court papers that it had defaulted on a $15 million loan it had taken in 2017.

LeClairRyan in 2018 created a joint venture with alternative legal services provider UnitedLex, promising a new model for supporting law firm operations that could expand to other firms. The Chapter 7 trustee who is overseeing LeClairRyan's bankruptcy estate has alleged that the UnitedLex deal caused already-struggling LeClairRyan to plunge "further into insolvency."

Prior to the defections, LeClair had about 270 lawyers and $122 million in revenue in 2018. The firm's bankruptcy proceedings are still ongoing.

DEWEY & LEBOEUF

Dewey, which once had close to 1,400 lawyers, went bankrupt in May 2012, unable to pay for the lavish compensation packages it had promised to recruit star partners.

The Manhattan District Attorney began investigating the law firm's executives one month before it filed for bankruptcy, after a group of partners asked the prosecutor's office to examine "financial irregularities" at the firm.

The office brought charges against several Dewey executives in 2014, alleging that they used illegal accounting adjustments between 2008 and 2012 to conceal the firm's financial difficulties from investors in its bonds, including Bank of America Corp and HSBC Holdings Plc.

Seven lower-level employees pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with the investigation. The firm's former chairman struck a deal with prosecutors to resolve his case, while its former chief financial officer was convicted of defrauding the firm's investors but avoided prison time.

HOWREY

Proceedings related to the liquidation of Washington, DC-founded Howrey are still ongoing after the firm's partners voted to dissolve the firm in March 2011.

The firm, co-founded in 1956, had about 750 lawyers at its peak in 2008. One month after the firm's partners voted to wind down, a small group of creditors tried to force Howrey into bankruptcy against its will.

Howrey later asked a bankruptcy judge in San Francisco to convert the involuntary bankruptcy petition into a voluntary case. The firm revealed it owed $49 million to Citibank, as well as $12.7 million in rent to its landlords.

data.title: Corn, soy bids mixed amid harvest progress
data.description:
Basis bids for corn and soybeans were mostly steady to mixed in the US Midwest on Friday as producers focused on harvesting the remaining corn and soybean crop.

  • The corn and soybean harvest has continued at a steady clip, though rains forecast through the weekend and early next week may slow progress.

  • Corn futures fell, with the most-active contract notching a fifth consecutive weekly loss on growing US harvest supplies and fund liquidation as traders adjusted positions ahead of month end, analysts said.

  • CBOT soybeans ended the day mixed on bargain-buying and signs of export demand, with deferred months ending lower. While the most-active contract was up for much of the session, it eased late in the day and marked a third straight weekly loss.

  • Exporters sold 165,150 metric tons of US soybeans received in the reporting period to unknown destinations for 2026/27 delivery, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system on Friday. USDA also reported that an additional 132,000 tons of US soybeans were sold to unknown destinations for the 2026/2027 marketing year.

  • CBOT corn settled down 3-1/2 cents at $4.47-3/4 per bushel, as the contract has fallen about 15% over the past five weeks. CBOT soybeans closed down 1/2 cent at $12.34-1/4 a bushel.

data.title: Petrobras refineries run at 98% capacity in October, director says
data.description:
By Rodrigo Viga Gaier

Brazilian state-run oil firm Petrobras' refineries operated at a 98% utilization rate in October, close to the 99% recorded in the third quarter, as it seeks to reduce the need for imports, a director of the company said.

The refineries continue to operate near their maximum capacity, while complying with safety standards, the director of industrial processes and products at Petrobras, William Franca, told Reuters in an interview late Thursday.

  • Petrobras only carried out "a few minor" necessary shutdowns across the refining system in the period, such as at RNEST refinery, he said

  • Since the beggining of the war in the Middle East, Petrobras has ramped up oil output to capitalize on higher Brent prices, and hiked refinery operations to cut fuel imports

  • Petrobras' refinery utilization rate is expected to remain high and close to the operational limit in November and December, according to Franca

  • Petrobras will adjust its refining mix in December, he said, hiking gasoline production to meet Brazil's summer demand, and cutting diesel output after the summer planting season

  • In the first half of 2027, the refinery operation rate is seen falling to around 96% due to scheduled maintenance and expansion works at Replan refinery in March and April, he added
